generation.explanation: A Galton board drops balls through a triangular array of pegs; at each peg a ball deflects left or right with equal probability, so after n rows its final bin is X = number of right turns. Since X counts 'successes' in n independent fair coin flips, X ~ Binomial(n, 1/2), and the ball stacks converge to the predicted curve P(X=k) = C(n,k)/2^n — a beautiful demonstration of the central limit theorem in action. Use the controls to start the flow of balls, change the number of rows, adjust speed, or reset.
